themes.title: GCC sovereign AI push: Mistral-HUMAIN, quantum, data centres
themes.summary: Mistral AI and Saudi HUMAIN are collaborating to advance sovereign AI in the Gulf, while parallel tracks see new quantum-computer builds in Saudi Arabia and UAE-backed expansion of AI-ready data centres into Africa. Gulf capital is securing control of the full AI stack, from foundation models to on-prem and quantum compute.
themes.angle: For Gulf boards, 'sovereign AI' is moving from policy slogan to signed contracts, and the Gulf may be the fastest region outside the US to own the entire stack.

themes.angle: Leaders are capturing margin by owning silicon, a signal Gulf enterprises should weigh when pricing AI spend.

themes.title: Saudi-France rapprochement deepens from defence to AI
themes.summary: Saudi Arabia and France signed roughly 21 agreements spanning trade, AI, defence, mining and culture, alongside Aramco's potential $3.7bn deals and a growing $19bn-plus French investment footprint, headlined by a $7bn theme-park venture near Paris. The reset hands Riyadh an alternative supplier of AI and defence technology beyond the US.
themes.angle: The Gulf is diversifying AI and defence sourcing from sole US dependence, so boards should track the Franco-Saudi corridor.

themes.title: AI-agent economics: enterprise spend climbs on infra and too
themes.summary: ClickHouse passed $350 million in annual recurring revenue on OpenAI and agent workloads, an AI restructuring at WiseTech drove an output surge and the end of manual coding in areas, and Meta is preparing an AI agent platform. Enterprise spend is shifting to the infrastructure and product surfaces agents actually consume.
themes.angle: Companies that rebuild around agents show measurable unit-economics gains, not just press release promise.

themes.angle: US political risk on the AI buildout may lift the sector's risk premium, a factor Gulf allocators should weigh.

The supply chain asymmetry over AI hardware is fast becoming a board-level variable for Grenada.
themes.angle: Compute sourcing for GCC data centres is now a geopolitical variable, not just a procurement line.

themes.title: AI safety, cyber and influence defense
themes.summary: OpenAI says it disrupted a Russian covert influence operation using AI to project a fake think tank and a 'sovereignty' index, ex-Googlers launched a nonprofit to keep humans in the loop, and researchers warn AI is each lowering the barrier for state-backed attacks on critical infrastructure. Trust and security risk now sits at the exec table.
themes.angle: For security-conscious Gulf enterprises, AI trust and resilience is board-level risk, not an IT concern.
